perennials/ead560f:
"Blooming today" was the only label in that row phrased as a description
of the plant rather than as a command, so it read like the app telling you
something. It is a toggle, and a toggle labelled with a claim is worse than
ambiguous: pressed could plausibly mean the guide had decided the plant was
in flower.

"Mark blooming today" cannot be misread as a fact, and it keeps "today",
which is load-bearing: markToday always stamps the current day. The label
stays identical in both states; the fill, the primary styling and
aria-pressed carry pressed-ness, and a label that swaps on press is the
thing that actually confuses people.
noodles/ea5cabe:
Two-finger pinch on the timeline had drifted into feeling broken: it
fought the browser's native pan (touch-action: pan-x ate the gesture),
it rebuilt the whole arrangement DOM every frame, and it zoomed around
the left edge so the bars slid out from under your fingers. And a
one-finger touch on a lane dropped a clip immediately, so you couldn't
drag to scroll without littering clips.

attachArrGestures takes full control (touch-action: none). One finger
taps to drop a clip or move the playhead and drags to pan; two fingers
pinch-zoom, anchored on the bar under the finger center so it stays put.
The pinch scales the existing content with a CSS transform and commits
real layout once, on release — no per-frame rebuild to stutter a cheap
phone. Clips and the loop grip already stopPropagation, so grabbing one
never starts a pan; tap-to-add moved to pointerup behind an 8px slop, so
a drag pans instead of dropping a clip. onRulerDown/onLaneDown become
arrRulerTap/arrLaneTap, dispatched by the gesture manager; the now-dead
barFromEvent is gone.

Verified with synthetic pointers: pinch 37->139 ppb at a 3.75x spread,
focal bar pinned with 0px drift, one-finger drag pans scrollLeft 1:1.
